doc.title: Elvin Jones — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Coltrane's 'Alabama'
summary: He recalls Trane writing and playing 'Alabama' after the church bombing.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: John Coltrane also, other than his musical influences, his music was also influenced by the events and the culture of this country, for example “Alabama”.
Well he wrote that after those kids got bombed in that church, that’s why he wrote that. The next day he was playing it. I said, “Oh boy” I just had tears running down my face.

It was a hard time in this country. It was a difficult time. Thank goodness you were able to express it in the music so that you could help other people feel that, and try to come to understand how tragic that was.
Yeah, that was a real tragedy.
